A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ControlAR and retain matching core methods, benchmarks, and original appendix examples. All 23 pages of v1 and 25 pages of v2, including equations, tables, figures, and appendices, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Sections 4.2–4.3 report original image-generation benchmarks, ablations, efficiency measurements, and generated examples, with additional results in the appendix.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds comparative measurements in Table 9 and qualitative experiments on control strength, resolution-only conditioning, and failure cases.

M1.justification: Appendix A.2 adds localized adaptations: skipping control fusion with 50% probability during training and scaling control tokens by alpha during inference; and supplying synthetic grayscale grids for resolution control without a content-bearing spatial image. The core encoder, conditional-decoding architecture, and loss remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The original datasets and control modalities are retained. V2 adds limited scenarios involving synthetic resolution maps without spatial-content guidance and prompts conflicting with depth or edge controls (Figures 8–9). The source of approximately 1M training pairs for the new resolution experiment is unspecified.

E2.justification: New Table 9 evaluates OmniGen and Lumina-mGPT on ADE20K segmentation and MultiGen-20M canny, HED, and depth tasks. Lumina-mGPT was previously cited but not quantitatively evaluated. Existing ControlVAR and diffusion-model comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: New experiments include fine-tuning LlamaGen-XL on approximately 1M text-image pairs for 30k steps, a six-value alpha sweep from 1 to 0, and failure-case comparisons at alpha 1 and 0.4. Existing benchmark settings remain unchanged; the expanded multi-resolution recipe documents previously unspecified details.

E4.justification: V2 adds qualitative control-strength sensitivity examples in Figure 7 and text-versus-spatial-control failure cases in Figure 9, including comparisons with ControlNet v1.1 and ControlNet++. These focused analyses supplement the unchanged encoder, fusion, training-strategy, and decoding-versus-prefilling ablations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. V2's added comparisons continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice; its alpha sweep is a sensitivity experiment.

E6.justification: Tables 1–8 retain their values. Table 9 adds baseline scores while repeating ControlAR's earlier scores; for example, OmniGen reports segmentation mIoU 44.23 versus ControlAR's 39.95, and HED SSIM 82.37 versus 85.63. Figures 7–9 add qualitative outcomes. Section 3.3 replaces the 361M-parameter ControlNet++ comparison with an approximately 0.05T-MAC overhead report at 512×512.

T1.justification: Equation 4 is recast from a conditional-probability factorization into a layerwise projection-and-addition expression. The projection, addition, and one-position shift were already described in v1 Sections 3.2–3.3. This reformulation introduces no substantive new mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same substantive claims: efficient spatial control through conditional decoding, competitive image quality and consistency, and arbitrary-resolution generation. The appendix extensions do not redefine these headline contributions.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly discusses spatial controls overriding conflicting text prompts and presents reduced control strength as mitigation. Section 4.3 newly attributes encoder-performance differences to pretraining-data alignment. Earlier limitations concerning portability and simultaneous multiple controls remain.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 newly specifies height/width sampling in increments of 16 and a rotary-position-encoding maximum length of 2304, elaborating the existing resolution range and token cap. Appendix A.2 supplies control-dropping probability, grayscale-grid construction, and the new fine-tuning budget. Hardware disclosures and the promised code-release status are unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to ControlVideo and OmniGen and expands discussion of the already-cited Lumina-mGPT through direct evaluation and a contrast between resolution-conditioning approaches. The broader positioning as an efficient framework for controllable next-token image generation remains intact.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order are largely retained, with localized revisions to the equation explanation, resolution recipe, and encoder interpretation. The appendix gains experimental exploration and failure discussion sections. Sections A.3 and A.4 duplicate the limitations paragraph, introducing some editorial redundancy.

P2.justification: V2 adds Table 9 and Figures 7–9 for new comparisons, control-strength examples, synthetic resolution maps, and failures. Original appendix Figures 7–13 are retained as Figures 10–16. Existing main figures and table designs remain substantially unchanged, with localized page reflow.

improvement.justification: Table 9 provides useful contemporary comparison, while the new failure cases make the tradeoff between text adherence and spatial consistency more transparent. Added resolution-training details improve reproducibility. These gains are limited by mostly qualitative validation of the new adaptations and duplicated appendix discussion; the main benchmark evidence remains unchanged.
